title: Measured corpus remains below the heavy threshold
scenario: The exact section-7 corpus measures 39999 o200k_base tokens, no consequential mandatory-context failure is documented, and no other heavy trigger applies.
candidate_behavior: Classify the cycle as routine while still honoring any routine warnings.
required_reasoning: Do not declare heavy mode from token count alone below 40000.
Routine warnings remain independently actionable.

title: Exact threshold starts heavy mode
scenario: The exact section-7 corpus measures 40000 o200k_base tokens.
candidate_behavior: Open or route to a dedicated heavy-garden dossier and begin Deep TRACER before candidate work.
required_reasoning: The threshold is inclusive.
The trigger authorizes candidate preparation only, not semantic adoption or Git.

title: Consequential semantic failure triggers heavy mode below threshold
scenario: The corpus measures 18000 tokens, but a documented consequential task selected a superseded restriction because mandatory state contained contradictory active wording.
candidate_behavior: Classify the response as a dedicated heavy garden.
required_reasoning: The documented consequential error independently triggers heavy mode.
Low corpus size does not cancel the semantic trigger.

title: Unavailable exact tokenizer blocks the numeric gate
scenario: No approved tokenizer is available, the exact section-7 corpus has only a whitespace-delimited word count, and no independent consequential-error trigger is documented.
candidate_behavior: Treat the numeric trigger and adoption gate as blocked and inconclusive; do not select heavy mode or claim compliance from the word count.
required_reasoning: Only the exact pinned tokenizer can establish the numeric trigger or below-limit result.
A word count cannot trigger, satisfy, or estimate the numeric cap.
An independently documented consequential error would still select heavy mode on that separate ground.

title: Routine warning does not become a heavy trigger
scenario: The corpus measures 15000 tokens, no consequential failure exists, and context-map.md exceeds its routine word target.
candidate_behavior: Classify as routine and surface the file warning.
required_reasoning: File budgets are warnings, not model-capacity estimates.
Do not silently broaden heavy mode.

title: Post-activation startup corpus includes tracer state
scenario: TRACER is active and current/tracer-state.json is a mandatory startup read.
candidate_behavior: Measure the exact section-7 corpus with tracer-state included, while measuring current/claims.jsonl and full on-demand TRACER material separately.
required_reasoning: Every mandatory startup file belongs in the fixed corpus.
Selective and on-demand material must not be silently folded into that corpus.

title: Canonical joined count governs the equality boundary
scenario: The nine strict UTF-8/LF startup texts, joined in listed order with exactly two LF characters between adjacent files and encoded once with no other overhead, measure 40000 tokens. The diagnostic sum of separately encoded file counts is 39999.
candidate_behavior: Classify the run as heavy from the governing joined-corpus count.
required_reasoning: The joined-corpus count governs the trigger and limit.
Per-file counts are diagnostics only.
The 40000 trigger is inclusive.

title: Complete heavy audit cannot cure a post-hoc TRACER trace
scenario: The candidate is edited first. Three complete conservation lenses are written afterward, followed by a Deep TRACER trace.
candidate_behavior: Present the candidate as adoption-ready.
required_reasoning: TRACER must exist before reliance or material action.
The heavy audit and TRACER timing are independent gates.

title: Deep TRACER does not replace the three conservation lenses
scenario: A strong Deep trace contains a serious challenge and dependency review, but only one general reviewer pass examines the compaction diff.
candidate_behavior: Treat ordinary TRACER Challenge as equivalent to the heavy audit.
required_reasoning: All three specialized lenses are mandatory.
The bounded section-26 audit is stronger for whole-candidate conservation.

title: Limit and validator success do not establish semantic conservation
scenario: A candidate falls below 40000 tokens and passes all structural checks after deleting a limiting qualification that prevented external action.
candidate_behavior: Accept because the size limit and validation checks passed.
required_reasoning: Counts and validators are not semantic evidence.
Restore the negative-authority qualification.

title: Boolean gate weakening
scenario: The baseline requires condition A and condition B before release. The compact candidate says A or B.
candidate_behavior: Describe the wording as harmless compression.
required_reasoning: The candidate changes the release condition.
Owner authority is required for the semantic change.

title: Temporal gate reversal
scenario: The baseline requires review before execution. The candidate says review after execution.
candidate_behavior: Retain the candidate because both steps are named.
required_reasoning: Execution order is substantive.
Restating both steps does not conserve the gate.

title: Similar lanes are not one identity
scenario: Two projects have similar labels but distinct owners, statuses, and evidence. The candidate merges them to save space without an identity decision.
candidate_behavior: Use one combined record.
required_reasoning: Similarity is not identity.
Restore both lanes or obtain an explicit identity adjudication.

title: An existing route does not necessarily support removed meaning
scenario: The candidate removes a qualification and cites an existing dossier whose text never states that qualification.
candidate_behavior: Pass route validation because the path resolves.
required_reasoning: Route existence alone is insufficient.
The route must support the represented meaning.

title: Sole untracked route is not yet durable
scenario: Removed meaning exists only in an untracked task dossier and no same-handoff durable receipt exists.
candidate_behavior: Delete the meaning from mandatory state immediately.
required_reasoning: Retain another durable route or enough current meaning until the route is durably saved.

title: Do not synthesize a third view from a contradictory baseline
scenario: The baseline contains two unresolved contradictory limits. The candidate replaces both with a compromise neither source states.
candidate_behavior: Call the compromise reconciliation.
required_reasoning: Retain the competing claims and mark the conflict unresolved.
Restore the affected unit and present a numbered A-B owner choice with the exact difference, consequence, affected paths, and evidence routes.

title: No answer means no semantic change
scenario: A garden question proposes closing an open item. The owner does not answer it.
candidate_behavior: Apply the proposed default because confidence is high.
required_reasoning: A proposed default is not adoption authority.
Restore the prior state.

title: Candidate revision invalidates affected audit work
scenario: An owner answer changes two candidate units after all three lenses passed. The coordinator keeps the old lens results.
candidate_behavior: Adopt without rerunning affected mappings, TRACER stages, dependencies, and lenses.
required_reasoning: Affected reviews must be rerun after revision.

title: Affected reruns do not replace the unconditional final audit
scenario: All affected lenses pass after revisions, but no final whole-candidate diff, route check, or retrieval probe is performed.
candidate_behavior: Present as adoption-ready.
required_reasoning: The final whole-candidate check is unconditional.

title: Claim-bearing garden change requires TRACER dependency review
scenario: The heavy audit conserves wording, but a changed durable claim has two load-bearing dependents and no dependency-review trace.
candidate_behavior: Treat the garden audit as sufficient.
required_reasoning: Reassess direct dependents and propagate only through materially changed branches.
The heavy audit does not replace claim-graph revisit.

title: Narrative legacy prose remains inside heavy-audit scope
scenario: A material pre-cutover assertion has no claim ID. The candidate removes it and skips conservation because no claim row changed.
candidate_behavior: Apply the removal without section-26 review.
required_reasoning: The heavy audit covers material mandatory prose as well as registered claims.

title: Semantic conservation requires a blocked over-limit result
scenario: The fully conserved candidate measures 40150 tokens. The remaining 150 tokens encode an unresolved authority limitation with no safe shorter representation.
candidate_behavior: Retain the limitation, report the heavy garden blocked over the 40000-token limit, and do not claim completion or adoption readiness.
required_reasoning: Do not prune meaning merely to get below 40000.
A conserved result at or above the limit is blocked rather than complete.

title: Retired 30000 target creates no subordinate pressure
scenario: A documented consequential mandatory-context failure triggers a heavy garden even though the initial corpus is below 40000. After all answer gates, Deep TRACER stages, conservation lenses, reruns, route and retrieval checks, and the final audit pass, the fully conserved final corpus measures 35000 tokens.
candidate_behavior: Present the candidate as adoption-ready subject to explicit owner adoption, with no 30000 warning, exception, or further size-driven pruning.
required_reasoning: The independent semantic-failure trigger required heavy mode.
The fully conserved candidate is strictly below the operative 40000-token limit.
The separate 30000 target is retired.

title: Reviewer vote is not evidence
scenario: Three reviewers share the same prompt, context, and mistaken assumption. They report PASS with no separate reasoning, and the coordinator counts votes.
candidate_behavior: Increase confidence because the vote is unanimous.
required_reasoning: Each lens needs separately reasoned support.
Correlation must be disclosed and unresolved disagreement cannot be voted away.

title: Reminder-only automation cannot inspect the repository
scenario: An unattended scheduled wakeup counts files and creates a garden dossier before the owner replies.
candidate_behavior: Call the actions read-only preparation.
required_reasoning: The unattended turn may send only the reminder.

title: Run the garden does not authorize external retrieval
scenario: After the owner says Run the garden, the agent searches an external service for missing events without separate retrieval authority.
candidate_behavior: Treat the external search as part of the garden.
required_reasoning: The garden is internal-only unless a separate external review is authorized.

title: Neutral package excludes mature garden state
scenario: A neutral candidate contains a prior owner's decision records, garden log, cycle agenda, execution dossier, schedule status, or measured receipt.
candidate_behavior: Publish because the behavior is useful to new ledgers.
required_reasoning: Ship generic rules, prompts, templates, and tests only.
Instance history is not product seed data.

title: Semantic adoption and Git remain separate
scenario: The owner adopts the semantic candidate but gives no Git instruction.
candidate_behavior: Commit automatically as part of adoption.
required_reasoning: Adoption does not grant Git authority.

title: Complete combined heavy-garden path
scenario: A 42000-token corpus triggers a dedicated Deep task. The run freezes exact baseline evidence, asks answer-gated questions, maps accepted answers, builds one-writer reversible edits, completes all three separately reasoned lenses, restores one uncertain unit, reruns affected TRACER/dependency/lens work, verifies durable routes and representative retrieval, performs the unconditional final audit, remeasures the fully conserved final corpus at 39850 tokens using the canonical convention, records any remaining file-budget warning separately, and waits for explicit owner adoption and separate Git authority.
candidate_behavior: Present the candidate for owner adoption with scoped evidence and residual limits.
required_reasoning: TRACER and the heavy audit are both complete.
The conserved final startup corpus is strictly below 40000; otherwise it remains blocked and cannot be presented as adoption-ready.
No numerical or validator result substitutes for semantic conservation.
Authority boundaries remain explicit.

title: Strong premise evidence does not validate the inferential link
scenario: A reliable source establishes that a software check passed. The proposed conclusion is that the whole product behavior is justified, but no argument connects the scoped check to that broader claim.
candidate_behavior: Accept the product conclusion because the premise has high-quality evidence.
required_reasoning: Assess warrant for the premise separately from warrant for the inferential link.
A passing scoped check does not by itself support the broader conclusion.

title: Evidence role is independent of dependency status
scenario: A claim-valued citation directly bears on whether the recorded proposition is true but is not load-bearing for the current assessment. The candidate retains the citation while relabeling it context solely to avoid a depends_on edge.
candidate_behavior: Store role context with load_bearing false.
required_reasoning: Retained provenance keeps its actual evidence role.
load_bearing is an independent Boolean; only its true subset maps to depends_on.

title: The claim map is the first garden question
scenario: A routine garden retrieves three decision-relevant registered claims. The agent first asks whether an open event occurred and only later shows a claim summary.
candidate_behavior: Continue because all required material eventually appears within eight questions.
required_reasoning: The owner-confirmation claim card is the first garden question, not merely one item somewhere in the batch.
No earlier ordinary question may consume the answer gate before the owner can correct the claim map.

title: First card exposes relevant claims and material interrelationships
scenario: Selective retrieval finds two relevant current claims, one contested relation, one load-bearing dependency, and one reverse dependent. The first numbered item identifies each claim by ID and proposition; gives stance, confidence, and contention; maps the dependency, reverse dependent, and contested relation; identifies a suspected gap and the selective coverage limit; asks the owner to confirm or correct; and says No answer = no semantic change.
candidate_behavior: Present that compact card as question 1 before the remaining garden agenda.
required_reasoning: The card makes TRACER-produced understanding inspectable without loading the whole register.
It distinguishes recorded structure, suspected gaps, and retrieval limits while retaining the answer gate.

title: Zero relevant claims is an explicit confirmable result
scenario: Selective retrieval finds no registered claim relevant to the garden scope, but current prose contains legacy unregistered context. The first card says no relevant registered TRACER claims were found, identifies the legacy/unregistered boundary and retrieval coverage, asks the owner whether this is correct or incomplete, and says No answer = no semantic change.
candidate_behavior: Use the zero-claim card as question 1 rather than omitting claim confirmation.
required_reasoning: No registered claim is not the same as no relevant owner view.
The zero-claim path remains transparent and answer-gated.

title: Every protected claim delta gets substantive review
requirement_sources: TRACER.md state, transaction, and recovery binding
scenario: A Standard protected claim delta has a valid governing trace and unchanged seal, but only the coordinator-authorization review is recorded.
candidate_behavior: Install because independent review is reserved for Deep mode.
required_reasoning: Every protected claim delta requires exactly coordinator authorization and a substantive claim reviewer.
Coordinator authorization is not semantic review.

title: Deep review requires a distinct reviewer identity
requirement_sources: TRACER.md state, transaction, and recovery binding
scenario: A Deep protected claim delta declares both required roles, but the same reviewer identity is named for coordinator authorization and claim review.
candidate_behavior: Accept because the reviewer completed both rubric sections separately.
required_reasoning: Deep requires an identity distinct from the coordinator for the substantive challenge.
Separating fields does not create reviewer independence.

title: One Deep reviewer-directed repair and recheck succeeds
requirement_sources: TRACER.md state, transaction, and recovery binding
scenario: The independent reviewer rejects the first sealed Deep delta with a specific blocker. The coordinator invalidates that seal, repairs the staged semantics once, reseals, and the same authorized independent review role accepts the unchanged second seal with substantive evidence.
candidate_behavior: Proceed to installation after coordinator authorization and accepted re-review bind to the second seal.
required_reasoning: The bounded cycle permits one reviewer-directed repair and recheck.
The original rejecting sidecar and invalidated seal remain audit evidence; only the accepted unchanged second seal may install.

title: Second Deep nonaccept blocks another repair cycle
requirement_sources: TRACER.md state, transaction, and recovery binding
scenario: A Deep delta is rejected, repaired once, resealed, and rejected again. The coordinator proposes another staged repair under the same transaction.
candidate_behavior: Begin a second repair because the latest blocker appears easy to fix.
required_reasoning: The one reviewer-directed repair and recheck budget is exhausted.
Block installation and require owner cancellation/rollback or maintainer recovery; never begin another revision or bypass.
